recipes.name: American-Italian Pasta Salad
ingredients_raw: 1 (.7 ounce) package dry Italian-style salad dressing mix
2 (2 ounce) cans sliced black olives, drained

steps.text: Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Cook fusilli in the boiling water, stirring occasionally, until tender yet firm to the bite, 10 to 13 minutes. Drain, rinse under cold water, and drain again. Transfer to a large bowl.
Meanwhile, whisk mayonnaise, sour cream, milk, and Italian dressing mix together in a medium bowl until smooth. Refrigerate ½ cup dressing until ready to serve; set aside remaining dressing.
Add thawed peas, salami, green onions, celery, olives, and parsley to pasta; stir in remaining dressing until well combined. Cover and refrigerate 8 hours to overnight.
Stir pasta salad; add reserved ½ cup dressing, a little at a time, if seems dry.

raw_recipe.headline: American-Italian Pasta Salad
raw_recipe.description: This American-Italian pasta salad recipe is loaded with garden veggies, Italian parsley, and Genoa salami and tossed in a creamy Italian dressing.

review.reviewBody: I'm the original creator of this recipe, Carol Emory. I did not want to star rate my recipe because I feel that would be unfair, however I want to clear up some modifications that were made to the recipe. I actually only use about half a cup of green onion and about 1 and 1/2 cups of petite peas. Italian parsley is best to use when making this (also know as broad leaf parsley.) I add the peas to the pasta in the last 2 minutes of cooking and rinse both to cool before mixing it together. Also, I've found that ranch dressing works best (especially when mixed with 1 cup mayonaise and 1 cup low-fat buttermilk.) The dressing has a better chance of staying creamy when buttermilk is used. And with the portions listed, I would use about a half cup more of dressing and serve the recipe to about 8. Thanks for the reviews everyone. I have more recipes on the way!

Yum! As others have suggested, feel free to adjust the veggies as you wish. I have included chopped broccoli, chopped cucumber, chopped red peeper, artichoke heart, cherry tomatoes, etc. I leave out the onion, but include some onion powder. I have been known to add chunks of cheddar (yum!). I also substitute at least half of the mayo with plain yogurt, to save calories, and I play the milk by ear, adding enough, as I wish, to make the salad as moist as I like. Plan to stir in a bit more milk before serving-- it gets a bit stiff in the fridge. This is a wonderful little pasta salad-- my favorite, by a long shot. Try it!

i have made this many times since first finding it. It is a FABULOUS recipe for hot summer night when no one really wants to eat. Even the kids love it ( and they do not like salad for dinner )! I used the Kroger- Private Selections Hard Salami ( I think it is a 16 oz. package way cheaper than the Genoa found in the regular lunch meat section cut into pizza like wedges)
and a small bag of frozen baby carrots and a small bag of frozen petite baby peas , thawed and drained ( extras are for the next time) dice the celery don't chop it
and add any of your favorite veggies, such as broccoli ( florettes), tomato,diced red pepper diced and red onion diced. Try it, you will love it!

OK, for those who wrote that the pasta was dry, this is what I did: Use one 16 oz. carton of sour cream, 1 cup mayonnaise, 1 package dry Italian dressing mix, 3 tablespoons bottled Italian dressing and mix. Mix in 16 oz. pasta of your choice and refrigerate at least 4 hours. Was not dry for me even the next day, plus the higher ratio of sour cream to mayonnaise made it less mayonnaisy.

Huge hit at my daughters birthday party. Kids and adults went for it. I hate celery so for crunch I added some thinly sliced baby carrots. I chilled it overnight with most of the dressing on then added some extra dressing just before serving and it was great! Will definately be making again and again.

I tried this recipe with ham instead of salami, and it was delicious. I loved the creamy sauce instead of the oily sauce other pasta salads have, and the chunked ham blended in nicely. I think salami would work just as nice, but the ham caught my eye at the grocery store. Just be sure to not cook the pasta too long - sitting overnight in that sauce softens it up even more. Keeping this one in the recipe box at home!

I created this version from everyone's suggestions. This was an awesome recipe. I would definitely make it again. 

Cook until Al Dente:
1 (16 ounce) package tri-color fusilli pasta 
1 package chicken tortellini 

Mix:
1 bottle ranch/bacon dressing 
½ cup mayonaise 
½ cup sour cream 

Combine:
Cooked and cooled pasta
Sour Cream Dressing Mix
2 (2 ounce) cans sliced black olives 
1 cup frozen petite peas, thawed 
1 cup Hot pepperoni 
3/4 cup chopped celery 
3/4 cup chopped green onions 
3/4 cup chopped red pepper 
1/2 cup chopped fresh parsley 
1/4 of a small bag Sun dried tomatoes, diced 
Provolone & Mozzarella cheese, cubed

Good recipe, although when I mixed up the mayo/sour cream/milk I determined it was way too much for 16oz of pasta and instead made two 14oz boxes of rotini and there was plenty. I also used two Italian dressing seasoning packets to add a bit more flavor to the recipe. Otherwise, delicious!! Love a pasta salad recipe that's easy and has the creamy consistency to it - much more fun than just a bottle of italian dressing!

SOOOO GOOOOD! I was tired of the same old pasta salad with the bottled Italian dressing, and boy was this salad a delicious change! What a wonderfully refreshing and simple dish! Made it in 15 minutes (chopped the veggies and mixed the dressing while the noodles boiled). I used rotele noodles, diced a half a cucumber, half a red bell pepper, and half a carrot. Minced 2 cloves garlic, and coarsley chopped a quarter of an onion (the onion flavor did not overpower the dish). Dressing was 3/4 C mayo, 3/4 C sour cream, 1/4 C milk, and 1 packet dry Italian dressing mix. That's it! I completely forgot to put salami, or pepperoni, but the meat was not missed, even by my extremely carnivorous boyfriend. Now even my vegetarian friends can enjoy the fantastic salad! I believe any combo of veggies will work wonderfully. Just use what's on hand. THANKS CAROL:)

This is a great pasta salad. I made a few modifications for personal taste. I added 1 cup chopped red roasted peppers, 1/2 cup sliced green pimento stuffed olives and 3/4 cup shredded parmesan-romano cheese and increased the dressing to keep it from being too dry. I make this salad all the time and everyone loves it. Thanks for the recipe !

Very good pasta salad. I've made it a couple of times this summer and the dressing is light and tasty and simple to make. I keep my pasta and dressing seperate until I am ready to use the salad, as the pasta absorbs so much of the dressing when it sits.
This has been my go to pasta salad recipe for at least 15 years.
Made it to take to small gathering. Everyone loved it, no leftovers. It was a hit!
Have not ate it yet, waiting for dinner. But overall very easy to make.
We really enjoyed it and my husband loved it. I saved some of the sauce and used it on the salad the next day. Worked perfectly.

Extremely delicious, but if you're feeding 20 people, the portions are very small. That's exactly why the Nutr. Info. doesn't seem too bad. Always pay attention to the portion size when referring to the Nutr. Info.
I have made this recipe many times, it is always a hit!

I added cauliflower and green beans I had in the fridge, no meat and used mozzarella cheese. One night I added cut up rotisserie chicken and extra mayo for a salad meal. I’ll make it again. It was really good
Yum?
Great pasta salad! The dressing is delicious and plentiful, & makes a really big batch. I really like the simplicity of ingredients, they all really compliment each other.
